messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P0 - Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts for private inference-gateway (us-west-2). Start: 2026-03-14T15:23:03Z. Pager: @liam_oncall. Affected customers: some Dedicated + Private clusters. See /incidents/1819876543 for thread.
liam_oncall: on it. initial symptoms?
maria_support: seeing large spike in 502/504 across private endpoints. UI shows 30-40% error rate starting ~15:20 UTC. Customers reporting inference timeouts.
liam_oncall: logs show backend gateway returning 502 for many requests. grabbing gateway logs now.
sara_infra: adding — from vpc flow logs: a TON of TCP RST/ICMP from NAT gateway EIP during spike, lots of ephemeral port reuse. Suspect NAT port exhaustion or NACL blocking ephemeral replies.
kevin_net: +1. I see a config change in cfg-mgmt yesterday that tightened egress NACL on the peering VPC to allow only 1024-2048 for a subset of hosts (ugh). That would break ephemeral return flows for long-tail model caching traffic.
liam_oncall: can you paste the NACL diff?
kevin_net: here:
```
- 100 allow tcp 0.0.0.0/0 1024-65535
+ 100 allow tcp 0.0.0.0/0 1024-2048
```
liam_oncall: yikes. who deployed that?
sara_infra: rollout by infra-config yesterday 22:10 UTC to tighten ephemeral ranges. change request #INC-9834
ryan_sre: that matches timeline. traffic pattern: model KV cache warmups create many concurrent outbound connections -> NAT needs many ephemeral ports. If NACL restricts the range, conntrack port reuse causes resets and gateway 502s.
maria_support: customers impacted: onboarding accounts and some high-throughput dedicated pools. severity = P0.
liam_oncall: immediate mitigation: revert NACL change and provision secondary NAT to drain. Kevin, can you revert NACL to 1024-65535? If not, add a rule to explicitly allow 1024-65535.
kevin_net: on it. reverting now.
ops-bot: runbook 'vpc-nacl-ephemeral' invoked by liam_oncall
kevin_net: deployed rollback to NACL in us-west-2 peering-vpc. Changes applied 15:36 UTC. Confirming.
sara_infra: I'm adding a secondary managed NAT gateway and associating to route table for the inference subnets to increase port capacity. spinning up now.
liam_oncall: while that lands, any quick firewall appliance inline that could still block? check third-party firewall (TGW inspection) policies.
ryan_sre: checked TGW inspection logs — a brief spike of dropped connections correlated with the same time window; policy is fine now. Most likely primary cause was NACL change + NAT port pressure.
kevin_net: NACL rollback shows ephemeral ranges restored. vpc flow logs: reduced RSTs already.
maria_support: error rate dropping in dashboards — from 38% -> 12% in the last 6 minutes.
sara_infra: new NAT got provisioned and attached at 15:44 UTC. NAT metrics show free ports increased by ~3x.
liam_oncall: great. continuing to monitor. can someone run a quick connectivity test from a private node to external model cache endpoint (port 443) and show ephemeral src port range is preserved? paste output.
ryan_sre: test from node k8s-infer-02:
```
$ sudo ss -tna sport = :443
ESTAB  0      0      10.0.3.12:39321   54.230.12.99:443
ESTAB  0      0      10.0.3.12:39322   54.230.12.99:443
```
source ports are ~39321-39322, OK.
maria_support: customer-facing note: "We’re aware of elevated 5xx and timeouts affecting private inference. Root cause under investigation; mitigation in progress. We will update in 30 minutes." (sent 15:40 UTC)
liam_oncall: can we confirm there are no peering route table flaps? kevin?
kevin_net: route tables stable. route propagation to peering was delayed due to controller backoff during the spike; fixed on rollback.
ops-bot: automated alert: error-rate < 5xx threshold at 15:48 UTC -> cleared
liam_oncall: monitoring shows error rate now ~2-4% (baseline ~1%). keeping P0 until fully stabilized and we confirm no customer retries failing.
ryan_sre: recommend increasing conntrack table size on affected nodes and adding NAT scaling policy to pre-warm during heavy model reloads. Filing infra ticket.
liam_oncall: filed INFRA-2142 to add conntrack bump and NAT autoscale policy. Next steps: postmortem, revert risky NACL hardening until we have a safe rollout plan.
maria_support: making handoff note for next oncall. customers updated: "Mitigations applied; traffic restored; investigating root cause and next steps; follow-up postmortem to be shared." 15:55 UTC.
liam_oncall: handoff to night oncall @sara_infra — summary: P0 earlier today due to NACL change that constrained ephemeral range + NAT port pressure; rolled back NACL, added secondary NAT, increased monitoring. still watching for retries. full incident doc: link to /incidents/1819876543/postmortem
sara_infra: acked. I'll follow up overnight and coordinate with config-management to block similar NACL pushes without runbook signoff.
kevin_net: retro action: add CI gating for NACL range diffs on peering VPCs. I'll own.
liam_oncall: thanks team. closing active mitigation. keep this thread for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
